domain: organizational learning, knowledge transfer, analogical reasoning, and pedagogy
axioms: Reuse of a mechanism in a new context is a distinct and frequently failing operation, not an automatic consequence of having recorded it.
Agent topology is orthogonal to epistemic operation: moving knowledge across a channel is plumbing, re-contextualizing it is an operation.
Transfer requires structure mapping plus an explicit breakpoint statement; without breakpoints, false transfer is undetectable.
The receiving context has preconditions (absorptive capacity); a transfer contract that assumes a perfect receiver is untestable.
Knowledge shaped as a reusable procedure or worked example is a different artifact class from a validated claim.
Duplication against Compound and Orient must be tested at trace level, not settled by assertion.
primitives: propagation channel across agents, projects, and pace layers
failure_mode: Prone to smuggling multi-agent orchestration into the loop definition and calling a broadcast channel a phase.
Optimistic about transfer value; systematically under-weights false-transfer and attention costs.
Weak on epistemic separation: transfer artifacts easily acquire validated status as they cross contexts.
Under-generates disconfirmation and retirement candidates; transfer literature rarely models removal.
Its candidates cluster densely around Compound, risking synonym inflation rather than genuinely different operations.
